fade-out audio verification: For Audacity Fade Out applied to an entire track, compare the exported WAV against the source-derived expected duration/channels and inspect the amplitude envelope across multiple segments, not only first vs last 5 seconds, to avoid accepting unrelated audio or a fade applied only at the end.
audio mix/export verification: For end-to-end audio alignment tasks, duration checks alone are insufficient; evaluator should decode sources and exported output to PCM and compare the beginning and tail segments to confirm source content and order.
vm_file report parsing: When a task requires exactly N lines in a text report, parse the vm_file local cached path and count physical lines rather than filtering out blank lines, otherwise reports with extra blank lines can falsely pass.
end-to-end audio mix export verification: For audio concatenation/mix tasks, duration and non-silent RMS checks are insufficient; use decoded waveform correlation or fingerprint-style comparisons for the expected source segments at their required offsets.
plain-text report exact line count: When an instruction requires exactly N lines, count physical lines after handling at most one trailing newline; do not count only non-empty lines, because that allows extra blank lines.
audio concatenation/export verification: For tasks requiring one audio file followed by another, duration and RMS checks are not enough; decode the original and exported audio and use tolerant waveform correlation or normalized error at the expected offsets to prove the actual source contents and alignment.
audio concatenation export verification: For Audacity end-to-end alignment tasks, combine duration checks with waveform/content checks at the beginning and expected boundary; otherwise silence or a synthetic duration-matched WAV can falsely pass.
audio effect export verification: For audio transformation tasks, verify not only file format and peak amplitude but also that the exported waveform matches the source after the intended transformation, e.g. same duration/channels/sample rate and high correlation with source samples scaled by the expected gain.
audio concatenation and partial fade ver: For exported audio tasks, duration and non-silence checks are not enough; robust evaluators should load the source audio files, normalize sample rate/channels, and verify output segment similarity/correlation at the expected offsets, plus compare the faded segment against an expected fade envelope.
audio export content verification: For Audacity mix/export tasks, duration and RMS checks are not enough; robust evaluators should compare decoded waveform content against an expected transformed signal using resampling/channel normalization and segment-wise correlation or RMS error, especially around track boundaries and localized effects.
partial fade-in verification: For audio fade effects, avoid relying only on early-vs-late amplitude ratios; compare the edited segment against the original source with an expected ramp/envelope and confirm post-fade regions remain highly correlated with the source.
exported label text verification: For Audacity point-marker labels, exported label files should be parsed as local vm_file paths and should verify start time, end time, and text; for point markers, end time should equal start time within tolerance to distinguish markers from region labels.
WAV amplify verification: For Amplify-to-new-peak tasks, verify both the final peak dBFS and that every channel is derived from the source with consistent duration, sample rate, channel count, and waveform correlation; correlation alone does not confirm the exact gain.
Export Labels text verification: Audacity exported label files should be parsed as tab-separated rows from the vm_file cached local path; for stricter validation require exactly three fields per label row and reject extra non-data or blank lines if the task requires a single exported marker.
